chapter: Bebop, Tadd Dameron, Slam Stewart and Europe
title: Europe in 1947 with Slam Stewart and Erroll Garner
summary: The trio went to Paris with Coleman Hawkins, Howard McGhee and blues singer Chippie Hill; Garner had won a poll, and Collins met Nicole Barclay.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: And I would say Beryl, come on, B flat. She said, man, I thought it was B natural. She was a tremendous piano player. But any way she got ill and then Earl came with us, Earl Grant -- Earl Garner, what am I saying Grant, Earl Garner. As a matter of fact we went to Europe together, it was the first time I was in Europe with Slam Stewart trio, with Earl Garner, myself and Slam. And --

Oh, we went to Paris, and we played the Ambassador Club, we played a theatre, the [Marini] Theatre. It was on the Champs Elysees. And this package was Coleman Hawkins, and this was the first time he'd been back to Europe, since before the war. And Howard McGhee had a band, that went -- let's see, we had a blues singer by the name of Chippie Chippy Hill, who was a friend of my mother's, incidentally.
And she would curse these Frenchmen out and they didn't know what she was saying. She was pure earth, you know.

Then she called them (unintelligible). There have never been so many MF'ers in their lives. And they smiled, you know. But any way, Earl at this time had just won a poll. He wasn't aware of it, he had won a poll in Europe, as a pianist of the year, and we got there and they had everybody to meet us there, and it was just a fabulous -- it was the first time I met Nicole Barkley. You've heard of Nicole. A wonderful person, she really was. You know, she did an awful lot for musicians.
But any way we had quite a successful engagement, but we left Earl. They were just -- Earl was so big, they kept him over there, and we went back and Bevul rejoined us.
